Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Court restrains CLOGSAG’s 15th Quadrennial National Congress Source : GNA 23 November 2026 9:53pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The High Court in Accra has granted an interim injunction restraining the Civil and Local Government Staff Association of Ghana (CLOGSAG) from holding its 15th Quadrennial National Congress scheduled for November 23 to 25, 2026.
The Congress was expected to take place at the Pentecost Convention Centre at Gomoa Fetteh near Kasoa.
According to a statement from the Office of the Acting President of CLOGSAG, the injunction, granted on November 19, 2026, remains in force pending the Court's determination of the matter.
The statement urged all persons and institutions involved in planning, organising, facilitating, or conducting the Congress to fully comply with the court order and refrain from any activities prohibited under the injunction.
It said the court’s decision was intended to preserve the status quo while the judicial process resolved leadership and governance issues within the Association.
The statement further appealed to members to remain calm, exercise restraint and avoid any actions that could undermine the legal proceedings or create tension within the Association.
Members were also cautioned against taking the law into their own hands.
Mr Benjamin Arkaah Otoo, Acting President of CLOGSAG, called on members to remain united, vigilant and committed to the rule of law while the case remained before the Court.
The statement said the Association would share further information on the matter through its official channels.
